chunks: From him, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Ibn Muskhan, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about a man who gives in advance (sells) a young slave girl with known age and known color, and then she is given in excess of the agreed condition (or the price/value exceeds the condition), so he said: 'If it is upon the contentment of your soul and his (the buyer's), then there is no harm in it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on selling a slave with known attributes if the final outcome differs from the agreement?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* addresses the validity of *bay' al-wasif* (sale by description) for a slave girl, specifically when the final outcome differs from the initial agreement on age and color. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) validates the transaction provided there is mutual contentment (*tayyib al-nafs*), reflecting the Shia juristic principle that uncertainty (*gharar*) is mitigated by the parties' satisfaction with the actual delivered goods.
